title: Euro zone economy slows to 0.4% growth in Q3 as crisis-hit France contracts
description: Around 800,000 people demonstrated across France, including 250,000 in Paris, according to the CGT. The march in Paris began at 2 pm from the Porte d'
body: Around 800,000 people demonstrated across France, including 250,000 in Paris, according to the CGT. The march in Paris began at 2 pm from the Porte d'Italie and headed for the Porte de Vincennes after the route was changed by the Police Headquarters at the last minute. October 24, 2026. (Photo by Telmo Pinto/NurPhoto via Getty Images)Nurphoto | Nurphoto | Getty ImagesEconomic expansion in the euro zone slowed to 0.4% in the third quarter, statistics agency Eurostat said on Friday. The 21-nation euro area rebounded to 0.6% growth in the second quarter, following stagnation in the first three months of the year. The flash third quarter reading was nonetheless higher than the 0.2% growth that was forecast in a Reuters poll of economists. However, France's economy unexpectedly contracted by 0.1% over the July to September period. The country is grappling with soaring borrowing costs as investors balk at a political struggle to reduce its high deficit amid growing nationwide unrest over the cost of living. The European Central Bank voted to hold interest rates steady on Thursday, saying a shock from higher energy prices was not yet feeding into second-round effects in the wider economy. But analysts said the ECB may still opt for one more rate hike in December as energy costs remain elevated.The central bank also said that downside risks to growth had increased.This is breaking news. Please refresh for updates.

schema.headline: Euro zone economy slows to 0.4% growth in Q3 as crisis-hit France contracts

title: Some Polymarket user funds stolen by hackers; exchange referring matter to U.K. authorities
description: The Polymarket midterms 2026 website arranged on a laptop in Forest Hills, New York, Oct. 28, 2026.Gabby Jones | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesSome users of
body: The Polymarket midterms 2026 website arranged on a laptop in Forest Hills, New York, Oct. 28, 2026.Gabby Jones | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesSome users of prediction market platform Polymarket's international exchange had funds stolen from their accounts due to a hack of an unnamed third-party provider. Polymarket has contacted law enforcement and pledged to reimburse any affected trader. It's unclear how many users were impacted. The company's U.S. platform was not compromised.Traders first reported on social media platforms that they were seeing unauthorized withdrawals from their accounts on Thursday afternoon. In response, the company halted trading on its international platform. Polymarket said that it has fixed the issue on its end, and that trading resumed at 3 p.m. ET. It told users later in a chatroom on Discord that users who had less than $10,000 taken from their wallets will have funds restored by Oct. 30, and those with funds greater than that figure withdrawn will have to sign a release form to receive their restoration. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that the issue stemmed from a hack of DebugBear, a website performance monitoring platform. DebugBear in a post on X said that it was impacted by a security incident on Thursday. The person familiar with the Polymarket outage said that the company referred the matter to U.K. law enforcement, as that is where DebugBear is based. DebugBear didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. An analysis of publicly-available data by two analytics firms — Betting Intelligence and Polysights — provided to CNBC said that an account on Polymarket Thursday withdrew at least $2.7 million across 710 other wallets. "This is certainly a significant and new form of breach that we've seen on Polymarket," said Dan Zimmermann, the chief intelligence officer at Betting Intelligence. "The timing right before the midterms ...is certainly a wake up call for folks."Polymarket's international prediction market exchange operates as a decentralized finance platform on the Polygon blockchain and is not regulated in the U.S. The disruption comes just days before both the company's international and U.S. exchanges are expected to see heightened volumes during the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3. Back in June, a similar incident happened, when Polymarket said a third party vendor had been "compromised" and that the company would refund affected users. Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

schema.headline: Some Polymarket user funds stolen by hackers; exchange referring matter to U.K. authorities

title: Coinbase net income surges 66% in third quarter, benefiting from bitcoin investment gains
description: This photograph taken on Jan. 21, 2026 shows signage of the Coinbase logo during the World Economic Forum (WEF) annual meeting in Davos. Ina Fassbende
body: This photograph taken on Jan. 21, 2026 shows signage of the Coinbase logo during the World Economic Forum (WEF) annual meeting in Davos. Ina Fassbender | AFP | Getty ImagesCoinbase Global earned third-quarter adjusted net income of $719 million, up 66% from $433 million a year ago, largely due to a recovery in the cryptocurrency market. Coinbase said it earned $2.51 a share in the latest quarter, although it wasn't immediately clear if that compared with the 6-cent-per-share profit that Wall Street analysts had estimated. Revenue of $1.20 billion trailed the $1.233 billion expected by analysts polled by LSEG.Net income at the San Francisco-based platform surged thanks to the value of its volatile cryptocurrency investment portfolio, which can swing wildly even when the composition of the underlying holdings are little changed.   The third quarter value of Coinbase's crypto investment portfolio climbed due to a resurgence in the digital asset market. The price of bitcoin — often used as a gauge for all crypto assets — rose 39% in the three-month period ended Sept. 30 and the flagship cryptocurrency recently changed hands at roughly $80,809. Building beyond bitcoin In the third quarter, Coinbase deepened its push into non-crypto products and services, including artificial intelligence integrations for traders, tokenized real-world assets and prediction markets.  In July, VP of product Max Branzburg told CNBC that Coinbase would debut an "everything exchange" spotlighting tokenized stocks and other real-world assets, derivatives trading, prediction markets and early-stage token sales. The trading platform also introduced Coinbase for Agents in early October, supporting users that want to use ChatGPT, Muse or other AI agents to manage their portfolios or research and trade various assets. Coinbase also expanded its prediction market offerings, making a wider range of event contracts available to users. In the third quarter, prediction markets revenue grew to more than $200 million on an annual basis, while the number of traders on those markets increased 60% compared with the second quarter.

schema.headline: Coinbase net income surges 66% in third quarter, benefiting from bitcoin investment gains

title: Chevron beats earnings expectations as refining profits soar on high diesel fuel prices
description: The Chevron logo is seen alongside diesel prices above $7 a gallon at a truck stop in Commerce, California on August 26, 2026. Patrick T. Fallon | Afp
body: The Chevron logo is seen alongside diesel prices above $7 a gallon at a truck stop in Commerce, California on August 26, 2026. Patrick T. Fallon | Afp | Getty ImagesChevron on Friday reported profits that surged in the third quarter, as its U.S. refineries ran nearly at full capacity to take advantage of high diesel fuel prices. Chevron's net income surged nearly 200% to $9.9 billion, or $5.06 a share, compared to $3.5 billion, or $1.82 a share, in the same period last year. When adjusted for one-time items, it reported earnings of $5.28 per share, soundly beating Wall Street's expectations of $4.89. Chevron shares are up about 2% in premarket trading. Diesel prices have surged globally as Ukraine and Iran have bombed refineries in Russia and the Middle East. U.S. refiners have ramped up production to fill the supply gap.Chevron's U.S. refineries processed record amounts of crude oil at just above 1 million barrels per day, as the facilities ran at 98% capacity. Diesel and jet fuel yields rose more than 10%, the company said. Profits from Chevron's refining division surged more than 300% to $4.9 billion compared to $1.1 billion in the same period in 2025. Here's how Chevron did, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG:Earnings per share: $5.28 adjusted, vs. $4.89 expectedRevenue: $67.8 billion, vs. $61.6 billion expectedProfits from Chevron's oil and gas production rose about 70% to $5.7 billion compared to $3.3 billion in the year-ago period. Its output actually declined slightly to 3.9 million bpd compared to about 4 million bpd in the same period last year. The decline was in its international segment due in part to the conflict in the Middle East, while output was largely flat in the U.S. year over year.

schema.headline: Chevron beats earnings expectations as refining profits soar on high diesel fuel prices

title: BOJ holds rates as underlying inflation aligns with 2% target for first time since 2013
description: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) headquarters in Tokyo, Japan, on Friday, Dec. 19, 2025. Photographer: Akio Kon/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesBloomberg | Bloomberg
body: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) headquarters in Tokyo, Japan, on Friday, Dec. 19, 2025. Photographer: Akio Kon/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesBloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesThe Bank of Japan declared that underlying inflation in the country was "generally consistent" with its target of 2%, the first time it has made that assessment since adopting the target in 2013.Before this, the BOJ used to say that underlying inflation has been "approaching 2 percent."This comes as the central bank expectedly held rates at 1.25%, still at its highest level since 1995.The decision was split 8-1, with board member Hajime Takata dissenting. Takata had wanted the bank to hike its policy rate to 1.5%. The BOJ also upgraded its inflation forecast for its fiscal year 2027 to 2.6% from 2.4%, with the so-called "core-core" inflation forecast also raised to 2.7% from 2.6%. The "core-core" inflation strips out prices of fresh food and energy. It also flagged a risk that underlying inflation will deviate upward beyond 2%, saying that "firms' behavior has been shifting more toward raising wages and prices and there are various factors that could drive up prices."Describing this as a "hawkish hold," Krishna Bhimavarapu, APAC economist at State Street Investment Management said that the BOJ sees more hikes ahead and is increasingly confident that the target is being achieved through a "self-sustaining wage-price-consumption cycle."However, he also added that growth in the country does not justify rushing the next move. Bhimavarapu forecasts that Japan's third quarter GDP growth is likely to lose momentum, with consumption still the weakest link in the cycle.A CNBC survey of 16 economists before the decision revealed that all surveyed expect the BOJ to set the stage for a rate hike in December or January next year, as domestic inflation and wages continue to rise.Thirteen respondents said they expect a terminal rate, or the level at which the BOJ is expected to stop its tightening cycle, of 1.75% to 2% by around mid-2027.Japan has been grappling with a weak yen and high energy prices that have pushed up inflation. However, experts have told CNBC that CPI numbers are being held down by energy subsidies from the Takaichi administration. The most recent inflation numbers for September revealed core inflation hit their highest level in 2026, coming in at 2.1% and overshooting expectations. Earlier this month, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reportedly told parliament that Japan was "on the cusp of shifting to a period of sustained inflation driven by rising wages."Japan's inflation-adjusted wages rose for the eighth month in a row in August, climbing 1.5% from a year earlier, according to the most recent government data, signaling potential wage-growth-driven inflation as well.— CNBC's Lisa Kim contributed to this report.

schema.headline: BOJ holds rates as underlying inflation aligns with 2% target for first time since 2013

title: Starbucks sales miss expectations, but its U.S. turnaround is gaining steam
description: Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol speaks during the Starbucks Investor Day event in New York City, U.S., Jan. 29, 2026. Brendan McDermid | ReutersStarbucks o
body: Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol speaks during the Starbucks Investor Day event in New York City, U.S., Jan. 29, 2026. Brendan McDermid | ReutersStarbucks on Thursday reported mixed quarterly results as its international cafes underperformed expectations.However, its U.S. turnaround continues to take hold, as its home market topped expectations during the coffee giant's final quarter of fiscal 2026. "We enter fiscal 2027 with momentum, a clear set of priorities and higher ambitions for what Starbucks can become," CEO Brian Niccol said in a video shared on the company's website.Starbucks is ahead of schedule to meet the fiscal 2028 targets laid out at its investor day in January, he said on the company's earnings conference call.For fiscal 2027, Starbucks is projecting adjusted earnings per share in a range of $3.15 to $3.25, above Wall Street's expectations of earnings per share of $3.14. However, its anticipated revenue decline of 1% is weaker than expected; analysts were forecasting net sales growth of 1.4%. Starbucks is projecting North American same-store sales growth of 4% for the fiscal year. The company's earnings and revenue outlook includes an additional week and the effects of the shift in its China business to a joint venture business model. Starbucks is also projecting slight deflation in coffee prices and slowing net new North American cafe openings, which will both weigh on its full-year revenue, according to CFO Cathy Smith.Shares of Starbucks fell nearly 2% in extended trading.Here's what the company reported for the quarter ended Sept. 27 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:Earnings per share: 80 cents adjusted vs. 72 cents expectedRevenue: $9.14 billion vs. $9.23 billion expectedStarbucks reported fiscal fourth-quarter net income attributable to the company of $677.2 million, or 59 cents per share, up from $133.1 million, or 12 cents per share, a year earlier.Excluding restructuring and impairment costs and other items, the company reported earnings per share of 80 cents.Net revenue fell 4% to $9.14 billion, reflecting the joint venture deal in China.The company's global same-store sales increased 7.2%, fueled by growth in average ticket, and beating Wall Street estimates of 6%, according to StreetAccount. Transactions grew 1.8% in the quarter.Starbucks' U.S. cafes reported same-store sales growth of 7.7%, topping StreetAccount estimates of a 6.5% increase.Under Niccol's "Back to Starbucks" strategy, the company has focused on improving service, making its cafes more welcoming and sharpening its marketing. The changes have helped to win back customers."Starbucks brand affinity is at near record levels as our menu innovation, marketing and merchandise continue to create moments that drive culture and bring people into our coffee houses," Niccol told analysts.The company said its North American rollout of its fall menu, which includes the iconic pumpkin spice latte, was the company's strongest ever autumn launch day. And matcha is now a $1 billion drink for Starbucks.Outside of North America, the company's international comparable sales ticked up 0.9%, as traffic declines offset an increase to average ticket. That growth fell short of analyst estimates of a 3.2% increase, according to StreetAccount.After its China business transitioned to a joint venture, Starbucks has shifted most of its international business to a licensed model, allowing local operators to take charge. The company is also exploring selling a majority stake in its Japan business, Reuters reported in September.Starbucks opened 303 net new cafes during the quarter. In September, the company announced it would close about 1% of its North American footprint, or about 250 locations, as part of its turnaround.By the end of its fiscal year, across the U.S. and Canada, the company also completed more than 1,700 cafe uplifts, meant to make its stores more welcoming to customers. The company has said locations that receive a makeover, with tweaks like increased seating and softer lighting, see higher transactions in the aftermath.

schema.headline: Starbucks sales miss expectations, but its U.S. turnaround is gaining steam

title: Nvidia responds to report Jensen Huang was target of Chinese asset, says diversion allegations were 'investigated and debunked'
description: Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, presents new NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX Pod Full-Stack Modular AI Factory as he gives a keynote address at the Berlin GPU Tech
body: Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, presents new NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX Pod Full-Stack Modular AI Factory as he gives a keynote address at the Berlin GPU Technology Conference (GTC) on October 21, 2026 in Berlin, Germany.Sean Gallup | Getty ImagesAn Nvidia spokesperson on Thursday pushed back on a New York Times report that detailed American intelligence agencies surveilling a person close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang because they thought she could be a Chinese intelligence asset.According to the Times report, which cited people briefed on intelligence surveillance, Alice Huang, who is linked to the Singapore-based cloud Megaspeed, developed a close relationship with Nvidia's Jensen Huang. Intelligence agencies worried that she was a spy, helping the Chinese government gain information from Nvidia and Jensen Huang, and fretted that Nvidia's CEO had access to President Donald Trump. The Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the story in a statement to CNBC, saying that Singapore-based Megaspeed is another one of the company's regional cloud customers, and that Jensen Huang's interactions with its officials are not unusual, because he speaks with thousands of customers every year.The spokesperson added that customers don't get access to Nvidia trade secrets or relevant national security information. The report also alleged that Megaspeed was previously suspected of helping companies evade U.S. export controls on Nvidia's AI chips, which aren't allowed to be shipped to China.Nvidia said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls. "The diversion allegations against this regional cloud were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year," the spokesperson said in a statement. Nvidia implied that the U.S. government had not briefed Nvidia on Alice Huang. "We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," the spokesperson said. Nvidia has had to walk a tightrope in Washington as its AI chips have become a powerful tool for all AI developers and a bargaining chip in economic competition with China. Politicians and analysts say that Nvidia's AI chips could be used to create Chinese military AI models, or commercial AI models that could compete and eventually surpass American technology.As AI has become more important to the government, Nvidia's Huang has befriended Trump and has given pro-American speeches about building U.S. AI infrastructure. Huang has appeared with Trump at state dinners, AI summits, and international trips, all while pushing for certain Nvidia chips to get a green light to be shipped to China. Earlier this year the U.S. government cleared Nvidia's H200 chip to be shipped to China, but Chinese regulators prevented their imports. H200s are Nvidia's Hopper generation chip, not the current faster Blackwell generation currently used by American AI developers.The Nvidia spokesperson said the Chinese government is not looking for Nvidia products from regional clouds like Megaspeed. "Instead, the PRC government blocked U.S. AI chips, protecting its own industry and resulting in the largest write-offs in U.S. tech history," the Nvidia spokesperson said. Last year, Nvidia wrote off about $4.5 billion in Chinese-tuned AI chips.

schema.headline: Nvidia responds to report Jensen Huang was target of Chinese asset, says diversion allegations were 'investigated and debunked'

title: Amazon falls 7%, Intel plunges 25% in premarket trading, as pressure mounts after earnings
description: CFOTO | Future Publishing | Getty ImagesAmazon and Intel shares were down in premarket trading on Friday after they reported September quarter numbers
body: CFOTO | Future Publishing | Getty ImagesAmazon and Intel shares were down in premarket trading on Friday after they reported September quarter numbers that disappointed investors, dragging Nasdaq futures down 2% and capping off a week of rough tech earnings.Amazon shares were down 7% in premarket trading, while Intel was down 25%. Amazon reported a third-quarter miss on the top and bottom line while maintaining its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 of $220 billion this year. Amazon also reported negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, much larger than the previous period.Intel issued weaker-than-expected guidance, citing ongoing softness in the PC market.Chip stocks including Micron, Nvidia and Arm were lower in premarket trade in the U.S., while major European semiconductor names, including ASML, saw sharp declines.Stock Chart IconStock chart iconNasdaq Composite Index over the last 5 days. A tough week for tech earningsInvestors are nervous about the massive AI spending from the tech giants and whether that will pay off.On Thursday, Alphabet shares closed 13% lower, its worst single-day drop in history after it too reported ballooning negative free cash flow. Microsoft shares rose after it remained cash flow positive in the September quarter.Nasdaq-100 futures were down 2% in early trading as tech stocks remained under pressure, which could put the tech-heavy index into negative territory this week. Even with the recent fall, the Nasdaq Composite index is up more than 12% year-to-date as of Thursday's close. "I don't think this is a moment of reckoning but I think it's a moment where investors should take a long thought about how positioning across the space still remains crowded even though the fundamentals are strong," Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Friday."While the here and now can be painful … the fact of the matter is the fundamentals by and large still remain in place, especially across the AI capex beneficiary part of the market."Orton said he is "generally okay" with these companies turning free cash flow negative as it's for a "temporary period."

schema.headline: Amazon falls 7%, Intel plunges 25% in premarket trading, as pressure mounts after earnings

title: Biggest-ever crypto hack impacts $6.3 billion as Binance works to contain fallout
description: Circle signage during the company's initial public offering in front of the New York Stock Exchange, June 5, 2025.Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Im
body: Circle signage during the company's initial public offering in front of the New York Stock Exchange, June 5, 2025.Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesBinance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses.The company's co-CEO Richard Teng said the exchange would cover all losses from the $6.3 billion hack using its SAFU fund and company funds, with about $3 billion in stolen assets frozen on-chain so far.The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." Later in the day, Teng said the attack involved a complex process rather than the misuse of a single engineer's permissions, underscoring that the investigation had not attributed responsibility to any individual. He added that there was no evidence of any wallet private key leak.Binance has temporarily suspended withdrawals while it overhauls its withdrawal security systems and has revoked the affected address authorizations, Teng said. The exchange is also working with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover the stolen funds, while deposits remain unaffected.Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls. It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours.The exchange said it would cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds, adding that customer funds remained safe.Binance also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorization and enlisted law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover funds.The company said it would publish a technical report, and an updated Proof of Reserves after remediation efforts."We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified," Binance said.The announcement followed moves by several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group, Tether and Ripple, to freeze funds tied to the hack.Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,994.96 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets. Shares of Circle tumbled about 5% in after-hours trading on Thursday. "Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said. "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe." Binance also said on X that Binance Alpha trading had been temporarily suspended, and that "the current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion."Outside effortsCircle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident. USDT stablecoin issuer Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also said in on X that his firm had frozen more than 1.5 billion of its stablecoin that may have been related to a potential breach. Jack McDonald, Ripple's senior vice president of stablecoins, said it was actively freezing affected funds held in RLUSD, its U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin. Later, Yi He said in a statement that the XRP and RLUSD-tied firm Ripple helped halt the movement of $200 million of funds linked to the possible attack.  But those frozen funds could represent only part of those impacted. Crypto data provider Arkham Intelligence linked nearly $6 billion in digital assets — including bitcoin, ether, solana and various stablecoins — to 55 wallet addresses it has linked to the potential exploit.Arkham identifies, tracks and flags crypto wallets by analyzing publicly available blockchain data. It also solicits tips from its community members.Exploits are not uncommon in the crypto space. In 2025, Bybit suffered roughly $1.5 billion in losses due to a hack. More recently, Bitget lost more than $350 million worth of digital assets in a cyber theft incident. Over the past several years, bad actors have also drained billions of dollars in crypto from decentralized exchanges.

schema.headline: Biggest-ever crypto hack impacts $6.3 billion as Binance works to contain fallout

title: Trump, Vance scrap planned appearances in final stretch of midterm campaign
description: WASHINGTON, DC - OCTOBER 20: U.S. Vice President JD Vance (R) looks on as U.S. President Donald Trump speaks during an event in the Oval Office of the
body: WASHINGTON, DC - OCTOBER 20: U.S. Vice President JD Vance (R) looks on as U.S. President Donald Trump speaks during an event in the Oval Office of the White House on October 20, 2026 in Washington, DC.  Andrew Harnik | Getty Images News | Getty ImagesPresident Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance canceled several planned appearances across three states, in the final days of a midterm campaign that could see Republicans lose control of Congress.Trump canceled two weekend rallies in Kansas and Iowa and will instead hold a flurry of tele-rallies, addressing voters by phone. The Republican National Committee said the president would reach at least 19 states in a "72-hour sprint" before Tuesday's elections.The canceled stops were part of a midterm blitz in which Trump said he would travel to 35 locations to boost Republican turnout. He had been scheduled to appear in Kansas on Saturday and Iowa on Sunday."Voters across the country want to hear from President Trump before Election Day, and this 72-hour sprint will be a huge boost in the closing days," RNC Chairman Joe Gruters said in a statement. Trump has campaigned at 25 rallies this month and acknowledged the strain following a dense schedule of back-to-back rallies. Sounding hoarse in Corinth, Mississippi, on Monday, he said: "God didn't make your vocal cords to do a rally every day."On Thursday, after campaigning for Senator Darline Graham in Rock Hill, South Carolina, Trump snapped at a Reuters reporter who asked how he felt after weeks of rallies and whether he was tired of traveling. "You've been following me for two weeks," Trump, 80, said. "I feel perfect."Hours later on the same day, Vance also called off a Friday news conference in St. Cloud, Minnesota, on the administration's "War on Fraud," though the reason for the cancellation remains unclear. Vance, who leads the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, was scheduled to appear with other members to make an announcement on the administration’s 'War on Fraud” effort, according to the White House.The scrapped appearance came as Trump's approval rating has fallen to historic lows amid growing frustration over high gasoline prices and the prolonged war with Iran.Forecasters and prediction markets see the Democrats favored to sweep Congress, flipping both the House and Senate blue. The NBC News average of national polls showed 52% of surveyed Americans preferred Democratic control of Congress, compared with 43% who favored Republican control. Trump is still scheduled to hold a rally in Daytona Beach, Florida, on Friday, and no events have been announced for Monday, the final day of the campaign.

schema.headline: Trump, Vance scrap planned appearances in final stretch of midterm campaign

title: Foxconn hopes to own 50% of the global AI server market within a couple years
description: The logo of multinational tech company Foxconn (also known as Hon Hai), which is a major manufacturer for Apple products, in Taipei, Taiwan, on April
body: The logo of multinational tech company Foxconn (also known as Hon Hai), which is a major manufacturer for Apple products, in Taipei, Taiwan, on April 16, 2025.Anadolu | Anadolu | Getty ImagesTaiwanese electronics giant Hon Hai Technology Group, or Foxconn, is looking to expand its artificial intelligence server market share and boost manufacturing in the United States, as demand for AI infrastructure shows little sign of slowing, Chairman Young Liu told CNBC.In an interview with CNBC's Christine Tan,  Liu said Foxconn's share of the global AI server market could reach 50% in a couple of years, potentially rising to around 45% next year."I think we can grow up to 50 percent," Liu said, referring to Foxconn's share of the global AI server market, which currently stands at around 40%.watch nowFormally known as Hon Hai Precision Industry, the company is best known as a major assembler of Apple's iPhones but has increasingly turned to AI infrastructure as a key growth driver.Liu expects AI infrastructure to account for 60% to 65% of Foxconn's revenue in the next three to five years, excluding edge AI devices — which run AI and machine learning algorithms directly on local hardware.Foxconn's production capacity was already fully booked for at least the next year and a half, Liu said, pointing to sustained demand for AI infrastructure.He said demand so far has come largely from AI model developers and cloud service providers, while governments and enterprises have yet to fully embrace the technology. AI demand remains “quite strong,” he added.U.S. manufacturing expansionFoxconn is looking to expand its U.S. manufacturing footprint, with Liu saying the company plans to move further up the supply chain to better serve the U.S. market."What we are going to do is we're going to move up the supply chain," he said, explaining that a broader manufacturing presence would allow Foxconn to respond more quickly to rising demand.However, higher manufacturing costs in the U.S. mean the company will initially focus on products with stronger margins, including AI server racks and data center equipment.Liu said greater production scale in the U.S. could eventually help lower manufacturing costs.The expansion comes as Foxconn seeks to strengthen its position across the AI infrastructure supply chain, from servers and racks to entire data centers and computing services.AI spending risksHowever, even as AI demand continues to grow, Liu emphasized the importance of managing investments carefully."Overinvestment will kill the company," he said, adding that Foxconn would keep a tight rein on spending as it expands its AI business.Liu said Foxconn could spend more than its planned $3 billion to $5 billion a year on AI, depending on how far it expands its vertical integration.Asked how the company would respond if major customers cut back on AI spending, Liu said weaker demand from one customer could be offset by growth elsewhere. However, an industry-wide slowdown would pose a much bigger challenge for Foxconn and the broader AI supply chain.

schema.headline: Foxconn hopes to own 50% of the global AI server market within a couple years

title: Rivian third-quarter earnings beat estimates as software revenue, R2 deliveries rise
description: Signage outside Rivian's offices in Palo Alto, California, Dec. 10, 2025.Jason Henry | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesRivian Automotive beat Wall Street's th
body: Signage outside Rivian's offices in Palo Alto, California, Dec. 10, 2025.Jason Henry | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesRivian Automotive beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations as it ramped up production of its new R2 entry-level SUV that the company has promised investors will lead it to profitability.Here's how Rivian performed in the period ended Sept. 30, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:Loss per share: 48 cents adjusted vs. loss of 62 cents expectedRevenue: $2.16 billion vs. $1.99 billion expectedShares of Rivian were up roughly 7% during afterhours trading Thursday, after hitting a new 52-week low of $11.38 earlier in the day. The stock closed at $11.45 a share, down 1.9%The electric vehicle maker also revised its 2026 guidance to mark expected improvements in its vehicle deliveries, pre-tax adjusted earnings and capital expenditures.The new guidance calls for a pre-tax adjusted loss of between $1.75 billion and $1.85 billion — a $100 million improvement at the midpoint from its prior guidance — vehicle deliveries of between 67,000 and 70,000 units, up from at least 65,000; and capital expenditures of between $1.4 billion and $1.5 billion, $300 million less at the midpoint.Rivian attributed the improvement in its pre-tax adjusted earnings guidance to better-than-expected revenue related to its sales of regulatory credits, an IEEPA tariff refund receivable in the third quarter and its expected increase in vehicle deliveries.The R2 — the first deliveries of which arrived to customers in June — has become Rivian's best-selling model and was responsible for "much of the gain quarter-over-quarter," the company said. Rivian delivered a record 19,248 units from July through September. The company does not disclose deliveries by vehicle.watch nowThe EV maker remains unprofitable overall but continued to narrow its losses during the quarter. The company reported a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $913 million, compared with a loss of $1.17 billion during the third quarter of 2025.Rivian's gross profit, which is closely monitored by investors, was $176 million during the third quarter, up from $24 million a year earlier. Its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was a loss of $435 million, a $167 million improvement from the same period last year.The company reported that its software and services segment continues to grow, generating $605 million in revenue and a gross profit of $256 million, a 42% margin. That compares to its automotive operations, which recorded nearly $1.55 billion in revenue and a gross loss of $80 million.Also on Thursday, Rivian reiterated that it expects the R2, a smaller and less expensive sibling to its current luxury R1S SUV, to have a positive gross margin by the end of the year. CEO RJ Scaringe has said the company needs to scale beyond current R2 production plans of 160,000 units in order to achieve overall profitability."That ramp-up is critical for us getting to positive gross margin on R2 and that ultimately will contribute to positive gross margin for the business," Scaringe told CNBC's Phil LeBeau during an interview Thursday. "We're going to see that through the end of the quarter and the unit economics will continue to grow … into Q1 of next year as well."Rivian on Thursday said its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments balance was $5.5 billion, up from $5.3 billion to end the second quarter.watch now

schema.headline: Rivian third-quarter earnings beat estimates as software revenue, R2 deliveries rise

title: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in debt as it pursues AI buildout
description: The official logo signage is pictured on the exterior facade of a Microsoft Corporation office building in Lehi, Utah, United States, on August 26, 20
body: The official logo signage is pictured on the exterior facade of a Microsoft Corporation office building in Lehi, Utah, United States, on August 26, 2026.Charles-McClintock Wilson | Nurphoto | Getty ImagesMicrosoft on Thursday announced plans to raise $25 billion in bonds, taking advantage of its healthy credit rating to support its infrastructure expansion. The software maker holds a top-tier AAA rating with S&P, a credit agency. Management is targeting $170 billion in 2026 capital expenditures, as the company looks to meet heavy demand from artificial intelligence labs Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as other clients."Microsoft intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate purposes,  which may include, among other things, funding for working capital, capital expenditures, repurchases of capital stock, acquisitions, and repayment of existing debt," according to a statement. The offerings should close on Nov. 4, the company said. Amazon and Alphabet have engaged the bond market to support infrastructure projects this year, and AI-focused cloud CoreWeave has also relied on the debt market to broaden its data center footprint. Investors have turned more skittish on companies with tall debt piles as central bankers raise interest rates to fight inflation.Microsoft will access additional funding sources to complement its own cash flow generation when conditions are attractive, Amy Hood, its finance chief, said on the company's earnings call on Wednesday. "There's a form of financing called leasing, and we've been using that one as a vehicle," she said. "We're fortunate to have access in the debt markets, given where our ratings are, and we haven't yet tapped that."Microsoft reported positive free cash flow on Wednesday, differentiating itself from Alphabet, whose cash flow was negative for the second quarter in a row. Last week Meta said it had negative free cash flow, and on Thursday Amazon reported negative free cash flow.Also on Wednesday, Oracle unveiled plans to raise $10 billion in new debt and said it anticipates a return to positive free cash flow in the second half of its 2028 fiscal year.WATCH: We need AI token prices to come down, says Citi's Heath Terrywatch now

schema.headline: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in debt as it pursues AI buildout

title: BP’s third-quarter profit nearly quadruples to $8.5 billion as refining margins surge
description: watch nowOil major BP smashed third-quarter expectations on Friday, as volatile energy markets and high refining margins saw profits nearly quadruple
body: watch nowOil major BP smashed third-quarter expectations on Friday, as volatile energy markets and high refining margins saw profits nearly quadruple year-on-year. The company reported $8.5 billion in underlying replacement cost profit, used as a proxy for net profit. That was above the $6.191 billion forecast by analysts in an LSEG-compiled consensus and up from $2.2 billion a year ago. Operating cash flow hit $28.55 billion across the first nine months of the year, up from $16.89 billion in 2025, while net debt fell to $13.87 billion from $26.05 billion across the same period.The result primarily reflects better performance in gas and marketing trading, and "significantly higher" realized refining margins, BP said. "These are dynamic times with volatility and disruption to trade flows continuing to define energy markets," BP CEO Meg O'Neill said in a statement."The industry as a whole has been showing remarkable adaptability. Refineries have been running close to capacity to make up for shortfalls, shipping has been taking different and longer routes, and releases from strategic and commercial reserves are helping to bridge supply gap."Demand outlookRivals Shell and TotalEnergies on Thursday said their refining margins — the amount earned from processing crude oil into products like diesel, jet fuel and gasoline — hit historically high levels. Outages and damage to refineries from global conflicts, from the Russia-Ukraine war to the Middle East, have created tightness in global fuel markets this year, pushing product prices sharply higher relative to crude. Benchmark crude prices have also been hugely volatile this year as traders reacted swiftly to unpredictable newsflow coming from the U.S. and Israel's war with Iran, and remain nearly double their level a year ago. Stock Chart IconStock chart iconICE Brent crude price.Analysts have been questioning when and if high energy prices will ultimately drive demand destruction, easing pressures on constrained refineries, as the premium for refined products over crude remains at decade-highs.  BP CEO O'Neill told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Friday that BP's refining indicator margin for the quarter of $46.7 a barrel was "incredibly strong" and "indicative of demand for the products we produce," boosted by refining reliability of over 96%."We've been able to adapt and try to adjust our refining runs to meet... the needs for the product that is most in demand," she said."Now, if we roll forward, we are seeing refining margins start to soften a bit ... third quarter is always a big driving period and a big holiday period. So, fourth quarter demand typically drops off. That is bringing the refining margins down a bit." "But again, what we control is our ability to run our facilities safely and reliably to try to capture the opportunity that presents itself."BP announced a new strategy last year that sees the energy giant pivot back towards its traditional oil and gas operations and away from renewables. It also announced a consolidation of its leadership structure and debt reduction.O'Neill told CNBC on Friday that BP was focused on strengthening its balance sheet to give shareholders "confidence that they can be rewarded through the cycle.""So, oil prices today are strong. They will not always be strong. I've got 30 years in the industry, and the prices go up and down. And at some point, they will fall again. So we need to design a company and a financial frame and a balance sheet that allows us to reward shareholders through the cycle." That includes addressing its financial obligations, including the $5.9 billion it still owes the U.S. government and states for settlements over the Deepwater Horizon oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico in 2010, which it intends to ringfence extra cash for, she said."Deepwater Horizon was an incredible tragedy, and it has shaped BP. We will not forget the 11 men who lost their lives, or the impact that we had on the Gulf Coast and the environment there," she said."So we have deeply embedded those lessons, but we're in a position now where we want to take care of those financial obligations going forward to ensure we're a more resilient company in future years."

schema.headline: BP’s third-quarter profit nearly quadruples to $8.5 billion as refining margins surge

title: Steve Eisman gets more conservative with portfolio as AI trade nears 'tipping point'
description: watch nowSteve Eisman of "The Big Short" fame thinks the artificial intelligence trade is near a "tipping point," but he's not ready to outright bet a
body: watch nowSteve Eisman of "The Big Short" fame thinks the artificial intelligence trade is near a "tipping point," but he's not ready to outright bet against it yet."I've gotten much more conservative in my own portfolio. We have shorted against the box a whole bunch of our positions, so that our risk is much, much, much lower. But I'm not, like, net short any," he told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Thursday.Eisman's primary concern pertains to the frontier algorithm models, which are exploiting a climate of fear around their technologies, he believes, in order to set up a competitive regulatory moat against more cost-efficient products and to obscure some faltering fundamentals. Bigwigs in the tech industry have issued similar warnings.Anthropic left its latest revenue figures blank in its initial IPO filing, but Eisman believes they will show a significant deceleration from the prior quarter. Other figures in the report point to capital efficiency issue, he said.The ratio of revenue-to-equipment-expense was 2.08 in the second quarter and 1.7 in the third, marking a significant change in trajectory, Eisman said, citing an analysis he'd been given.Yet, Eisman said he was scared to make a definitive bet against the AI trade because of how intertwined it is with the market as a whole, calling it "impossible" for the technology sector to be siloed away from the broader equity market and the rest of the economy."So much of the market is on the other side, and it's still reading tea leaves. I think we're getting closer. I think the numbers from Google scared people," he said.Alphabet's stock tanked after reporting earnings on Wednesday, following a big pullback in its core advertising business as AI queries supplant internet search across its various products.Stock Chart IconStock chart iconAlphabet 5 day.Google executives said Wednesday they were running experiments to figure out what to do about it."It's worth noting the strong growth in AI mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we are seeing in AI mode," Philipp Schindler, Google's chief business officer, said. "Our ad experiments have shown promising results."Portions of Anthropic's recently filed S-1 struck Eisman as "extremely negative" in light of the fact that it didn't contain many metrics for the upcoming quarter that would give a clearer picture of the company's financial situation.

schema.headline: Steve Eisman gets more conservative with portfolio as AI trade nears 'tipping point'
